text:
Montreal comes in with points in nine straight games (7-0-2), though the Canadiens have taken only 50% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in that run. Their last game was a 5-4 overtime win over Utah after trailing by two, with Logan Cooley scoring three for the Mammoth and Adam Engstrom getting his first NHL goal. The Canadiens are without Ivan Demidov and Mike Matheson. Toronto, off three days, is 2-3-0 in its last five and lost 3-2 to Utah, missing John Tavares and Kirill Marchenko.

Montreal has controlled more of the play at five on five (52% of expected goals to Toronto's 45%), and our numbers have this one close, 3.34 to 3.16 for the Canadiens. The Maple Leafs' results are running ahead of their chances: a +7 goal difference on -7.2 expected, with finishing and goaltending doing the lifting. Montreal takes 5.4 penalties a game, which keeps feeding power plays. In net, projected starters Jacob Fowler (+9.7 goals saved above expected, meaning saves beyond what shot quality predicts) and Sergei Bobrovsky (+2.1) are on opposite curves, and Bobrovsky was at -13.5 last season. Montreal won the September meeting 3-2.

Nick Suzuki, on a five-game point streak, is at 78% for a point. Cole Caufield, who scored twice on the power play last week, is 41% to score. For Toronto, Auston Matthews and William Nylander are each at 40% to score, and Jack Roslovic has points in seven straight. Our under-the-radar pick is Josh Anderson, a third-liner with 3.1 expected goals in his last 10 games against a Toronto defense that allows the 7th-most chances per 60. We have him at 23% to score, a player to watch.
